rules.evidence: A home shopper can discover a considered product and leave through its detail page.
The weekly edit and product grid lead; category and search refine that outcome.
Search, category, result heading, product name, subtitle, and price appear before product actions.
The searchable-collection pattern, CharcoalTextField, CharcoalSegmentedControl, and NookProductCard are reused.
Category, query, result, save, detail, and bag transitions are owned by NookViewModel.
Result headings, selected category, saved control state, and detail navigation acknowledge actions in context.
Collection previews cover compact, standard, and dark; the Nook runtime journey begins on this surface.
A shopper can find a known object or recover from a query with no matches.
The labeled search field leads; browsing and recovery remain secondary.
The retained query and result count sit immediately above results or the recovery message.
The searchable-collection and empty-state-recovery patterns share the collection owner instead of duplicating a page.
Ready, results, and no-results states preserve the query until the user clears it.
Live result counts acknowledge input; the no-results surface explains retention and offers Clear search.
Ready and recovery previews cover both layouts and the runtime test executes search recovery.
A returning shopper can revisit products intentionally saved for later.
Saved products lead; browsing is offered only as recovery when empty.
The saved count precedes the grid and the empty explanation sits with its Browse products action.
NookProductCard and the empty-state-recovery pattern reuse the same saved state as Shop.
Empty and content states transition through save toggles without a separate data owner.
Count, selected save state, and the contextual empty recovery persist after navigation.
Empty and populated previews cover both layouts and runtime revisits the saved product.
Mina can resume saved shopping, inspect the bag, or check the latest order.
Current shopping activity and latest order lead; identity is supporting context.
Counts are embedded in their actions and delivery state sits inside the latest-order surface.
AgentDemoProfileHeader, AgentDemoEmptyState, AgentDemoStatus, and CharcoalButton compose the page without fake account rows.
Before-purchase and with-order states expose only actions backed by NookViewModel.
Saved and bag counts persist; order status remains visible and View order details opens the durable receipt.
Both profile states have compact and standard previews; runtime opens the receipt and returns to Profile.
A shopper can evaluate material, price, delivery timing, and then save or add the product.
Product evaluation precedes the primary Add to bag action; Save for later is secondary.
Product identity, price, provenance, and shipping appear directly before purchase actions.
CharcoalButton selected states and AgentDemoStatus provide shared action and confirmation behavior.
Ready, saved, and in-bag states are controlled by the shared NookViewModel product ID sets.
Buttons become selected and an in-context persistent bag message explains the next step.
Ready and in-bag previews cover both layouts; runtime saves and adds the product.
A shopper can confirm chosen items, remove mistakes, and continue toward checkout.
Order review and total lead to Review checkout; item removal remains local and secondary.
Each removal action sits with its item and the total appears immediately before checkout.
AgentDemoSurface, AgentDemoEmptyState, and the shared order-total composition support both states.
Empty and ready states respond to add and remove operations; empty checkout cannot proceed.
Removal updates the list and total immediately; empty recovery preserves Saved products.
Empty and ready previews cover both layouts; runtime reviews a populated bag.
A shopper can verify destination and cost before creating the simulated order.
Final review information leads directly to the single Place order action.
Recipient, address, delivery method, item count, and total are visible before confirmation.
The checkout uses shared status, total, and CharcoalButton compositions rather than new controls.
The review is entered only with a non-empty bag; back returns to the editable bag.
Confirmation advances to a durable receipt and clears the bag atomically.
The review preview covers both layouts and runtime verifies forward and back flow ownership.
A purchaser can confirm success, amount, item count, delivery state, and the next path.
Order confirmation is dominant; Continue shopping is the sole next action after reading.
Receipt ID and durable fulfillment summary appear before the continuation action.
AgentDemoStatus and CharcoalButton express the durable result consistently.
The confirmed product snapshot remains available after the bag is cleared and can reopen from Profile.
A positive persistent receipt replaces transient-only success and Profile retains the order status.
Receipt previews cover both layouts; runtime reaches it from checkout and again from Profile.

runtimeScenarios.testName: every app keeps its root route stable across tab selection
runtimeScenarios.evidence: The executable cross-app route test records Shop and Search target bounds, icon and label centers, and text baselines; holds touch on Search and proves only its pressed layer changes with geometry fixed while Shop remains the selected semantic and content owner; cancels once with no persistent effect; then accepts a fresh tap and asserts after one pump that geometry is still fixed, Shop is painted and exposed as unselected, and Search and its content are selected on the same single Page, stable root Page key, and ModalRoute.

runtimeScenarios.testName: Nook completes search, category, save, bag, and checkout flows
runtimeScenarios.evidence: The executable widget journey covers discovery recovery, save, purchase, receipt persistence, and return from the Profile order detail.

runtimeScenarios.testName: embedded details use a real route stack and system back
runtimeScenarios.evidence: The executable route test observes both Page entries during CharcoalPageRoute motion and verifies that platform back pops the nested Navigator stack.

runtimeScenarios.testName: top-level destinations restore their own scroll position
runtimeScenarios.evidence: The executable destination test verifies independent initial offsets and restores Search while the same stable root Route remains active.

checks.evidence: CharcoalTabBar keeps touch-down and cancellation confined to its transient pressed layer without moving destination bounds, icon/label centers, or text baselines, then atomically commits geometry, selected visuals, semantics, and content in the first post-activation frame on one stable root Route; product, bag, review, and Profile-receipt pages use the nested Navigator, system back pops real CharcoalPageRoutes, completion replaces obsolete task history, and destination scroll offsets survive tab selection.
Discovery leads Shop and Search, purchase decisions lead task pages, and Profile now gives shopping activity a clear purpose.
All visible copy describes shopper outcomes and real simulation behavior; developer rationale was removed from Profile.
Every inventoried state is backed by compact and standard production-page previews, with collection columns constraint-driven.
Navigation, search, product open/save, bag removal, and back actions have explicit labels or visible text and persistent state.
